title: Em-dash joins in the new attempt-log export text (build_attempt_log_text) — implementer-authored user-facing copy violating the RT em-dash ban (guard 9)
evidence: client.gleam:6779 and :6781 compose the clipboard export with ' — ' joins: `attempt.at <> " — " <> attempt.channel <> " — " <> attempt.outcome <> case attempt.detail { "" -> "" ... }`. The function is new in RC4.3 (git diff 96746ec..HEAD adds it) and its output is written to the clipboard via copy_refcheck_export_effect (client.gleam:6792) — the §7.7 'attempt-log export' the landlord pastes into records, i.e. user-facing copy.

The text is explicitly implementer-authored: the story spec says RC4.3 ships 'a plain clipboard copy of the attempt log (no dead control; RC4.4 upgrades the text + verbatim toast + timeline)' — so no spec string fixes this content, and the UX spec fixes no export text (grep of ux-reference-checking-v1-2026-07-29.md for the join/format: no hits). The RT em-dash pin (client/test/copy_test.gleam:308 no_em_dash_test) scans only copy.toast(code, ctx)/copy.page(code, ctx) outputs and never sees this composition — the carried intake warning #2 gap, and this PR's new site is exactly where it bites.

The five new success toasts with the same defect were already reported by the c3 architecture lens (copy.gleam:874-884); this export composition is a separate, unreported site of the same guard-9 violation.
impact: Landlord-facing exported text (filed or forwarded into records/emails) ships with ' — ' joins, breaking the 2026-08-05 user ruling that no em-dash appears in user-facing copy; CI does not catch it because the pin only iterates toast()/page() outputs.
recommendation: Join the export lines with a plain separator (e.g. ' | ' or ' - ') or extend no_em_dash_test to also scan the refcheck_* constants and this composition path, so the pin covers the gap.

title: New takeover audit callsite bypasses the canonical Tier-2 helper audit/escalation.fail_open, duplicating its observability inline
evidence: escalation.gleam:20-24 documents the Tier-2 contract: 'Every callsite that commits state and then audits should match on the result and route the Error branch through fail_open/4.' The sibling lifecycle writer in the same folder follows it — trigger.gleam:1177 `Error(err) -> escalation.fail_open(config.sentry, event, row_uuid, err)` (write_lifecycle_audit).

actions_handler.gleam:651-678 (write_action_audit, new in RC4.3, used by do_take_over) instead rolls its own capture: wisp.log_error('reference action audit failed: ' <> string.inspect(err)) + sentry_client.capture with event_type 'ReferenceActionAuditFailed' — reimplementing what escalation.fail_open provides (log + Sentry BackgroundEvent at LevelError with redacted error_kind), minus the parameter-redaction discipline: escalation.error_kind intentionally never forwards string.inspect(err) because pog debug output can echo query parameters, and the takeover/correct/substitute queries carry landlord-edited referee contact details (name/email/phone).

The audit POSTURE is otherwise correct per AD-16: takeover is Tier 2 fail-open (best-effort after the committed UPDATE — appropriate since it writes no status), correct/substitute audits are Tier 1 fail-closed inside pog.transaction (actions_handler.gleam do_correct/do_substitute), exhaustion follows the pre-existing webhook best-effort shape (webhooks.gleam write_audit_event, which predates this PR). The defect is only the missed helper, not the tiering.
impact: Minor: the takeover audit failure path duplicates the escalation helper and logs raw pog error inspect (potentially echoing referee contact parameters) to the server log instead of the redacted error_kind — the exact concern escalation.gleam was built to standardize; no audit row is lost that the helper would have written (both paths are observability-only), so this is a convention/deviation note, not a data-integrity defect.
recommendation: Route the takeover audit's Error branch through escalation.fail_open(config.sentry, event, call_uuid, err) as trigger.gleam's write_lifecycle_audit does, and drop the inline capture; optionally reuse it for the correct/substitute DbFailure audit paths' error logging (redacted kind instead of string.inspect(err)).
